title: Powered generators annihilating a supported perfect complex
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T\subset X$ closed with quasi-compact complement, and $U\subset X$ quasi-compact open. Let $F\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pc-derived-category] be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] with all cohomology stalks zero at points of $U\setminus T$. Then there are $s\in\mathbf N$, global section families $g_i$ on $X$ and $g_i^U$ on $U$, for $i\in\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$ [def-sc-derived-global-scalar], such that $X\setminus T=\bigcup_i D(g_i)$, $g_i^U|_{\top}=\iota^*(g_i|_{\top})$, and $g_i^U\operatorname{id}_F=0$.

proof.text: Use the affine principal-open basis and compactness to obtain a finite cover of the complement by principal opens contained in it. Mathlib: IsAffineOpen.exists_basicOpen_le and IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover. Index the finite cover by Fin t.card using Finset.equivFin. Restrict each top section to every open; presheaf functoriality proves that these families are compatible.

The open U is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Perfectness gives quasi-coherent cohomology. For each generator, the support of F is contained in its principal zero set on U. Apply the power-annihilation theorem on U to the identity of F.

Increase each annihilating exponent n to n+1: multiplication by the generator after multiplication by its n-th power is still zero. The positive power has the same principal open, by Scheme.basicOpen_pow. Restriction commutes with powers. This yields all three clauses.
